GHAR SAJAG — ENGINEERING / TECHNICIAN LIVE DIAGNOSTICS DASHBOARD
DESIGN-ONLY TASK
Do not implement code.Do not modify files.Do not create commits.Do not change product behavior.
Your job is to study the existing Ghar Sajag repository and produce a detailed implementation-ready design for an Engineering / Technician Diagnostics Dashboard.
Design a technician-facing diagnostics capability for:
first-time Hub and ESP32-C3 node installation;

commissioning and placement validation;

live field troubleshooting;

identifying whether a failure is in:
sensor/node;

ESP-NOW transport;

Hub;

journal/persistence;

Wi-Fi/backend;

web/PWA delivery.


This is separate from the normal caregiver/family dashboard.
The technician should not need to read raw firmware logs for routine troubleshooting.
Conceptually:
ESP32-C3 Node-> ESP-NOW-> ESP32 Hub-> Hub processing/journal-> backend-> PWA
The engineering dashboard must observe and explain this existing flow.
Do not propose a duplicate event-processing pipeline unless absolutely necessary.
Diagnostic test controls may be separate, but real product events should stay on the normal production path.
Reuse existing telemetry, protocol state, persistence, simulator and APIs wherever possible.

Do not redesign unrelated product architecture.

Do not weaken production security or authentication.

Keep caregiver/family UX separate from engineering diagnostics.

Prefer human-readable troubleshooting over raw logs.

Preserve existing event/session/sequence semantics.

Clearly distinguish:
product events;

transport diagnostics;

system diagnostics.


Do not invent telemetry that the firmware cannot currently measure.

If a metric is unavailable, identify what instrumentation would be required.

Inspect the existing implementation before proposing a design.
Identify:
Hub modules

ESP32-C3 node modules

ESP-NOW transport implementation

event structures

ACK/retry handling

deduplication

simulator

existing admin/settings pages

For every proposed capability, state whether it is:
A. already available;B. partially available;C. missing;D. available only in logs;E. available only in simulation/HIL.
Do not assume.

Hub:
online/offline

last successful backend synchronization

Nodes:

assigned room/zone

online/offline

battery voltage / percentage if available

last event

current health

Recommended health states:
HEALTHYWARNINGOFFLINECOMMISSIONINGERROR
Define exact rules for each status.
Avoid arbitrary thresholds unless existing implementation already defines them.
Design a chronological live diagnostic stream.
Separate events into:
A. PRODUCT EVENTS
MOTION

DOOR_CLOSE

HEARTBEAT

B. TRANSPORT DIAGNOSTICS

backend delivery state

Do not require every field for every record.
Design a readable trace for a selected event:
Sensor triggeredNode event createdESP-NOW transmittedHub receivedHub validatedHub persistedRules processedBackend queuedBackend deliveredDashboard received
Each stage should have:
PASSWARNINGFAILUNKNOWNNOT_APPLICABLE
Example:
Bathroom PIRMotion detected
Node event created PASSESP-NOW TX PASSHub RX PASSJournal persisted PASSBackend delivered FAIL
Reason:Backend unreachable
The UI should explain where the chain stopped.
Determine how each stage can be proven using current event IDs, session IDs, sequence numbers and existing logs/state.
If correlation is currently insufficient, define the smallest additional correlation mechanism.
Design a device detail page showing:
node ID

zone

firmware version

uptime

battery

RSSI

last heartbeat

last product event

current session ID

latest sequence number

retry counters

duplicate counters

failure counters

last reconnect/rejoin

Possible technician actions:
Send Test Event

Identify Node

Refresh Status

Restart Device

Recommission Node

For each action specify:
whether support already exists;

where the command should originate;

how it should be authenticated;

expected response;

timeout;

failure behavior;

whether it is safe in production.

Do not expose signing keys or security material.
Design Node -> Hub diagnostics for:
RSSI

retries

ACK failures

last successful RX

last successful ACK

communication age

channel info if available

Design Hub -> Backend diagnostics for:
Wi-Fi state

Wi-Fi RSSI

backend reachability

pending outbox depth

oldest queued event

last successful upload

last upload error

Only propose:
packet loss percentage;

latency;

average RSSI;

trend data;

if the system currently has enough measurements to calculate them reliably.
Otherwise state the instrumentation required.
Design a guided installer workflow.
Example:
Validate Hub

Validate Room1 node

Validate Kitchen node

Validate Bathroom node

Validate Main Door node

Validate backend delivery

For a PIR:
"Trigger Room1 PIR"
System waits for the correct node/event and then shows:
PASSNode C3-01RSSI -57 dBmHub RX PASSBackend delivery PASS
For a door sensor:
"Open the main door"
System must reject an event from the wrong node as satisfying the step.
Define:

timeout;

retry;

wrong-node handling;

duplicate handling;

offline handling;

backend-offline handling;

Final per-device states:

Design diagnostics so a technician can answer questions like:
Is the node powered?

Is it associated?

Is the Hub receiving it?

Is RSSI weak?

Is the node retrying?

Is the Hub ACKing?

Is the event being deduplicated?

Was it persisted?

Is it queued for backend upload?

Is internet down?

Did backend receive it?

Did the dashboard receive it?

For common failures, propose operator-friendly explanations.
Example:
"Node is sending but Hub is not acknowledging."

Do not attempt speculative root-cause certainty when evidence is insufficient.
Determine how the current simulator can support the engineering dashboard.
Design simulated cases for:

delayed ACK

The same frontend/API contract should work against simulated and real devices.
Avoid a simulator-only UI.
Design authorization for technician diagnostics.
Separate:
READ_DIAGNOSTICS
from privileged actions such as:
DEVICE_RESTARTDEVICE_RECOMMISSIONTEST_CONTROL
Normal caregiver/family accounts must not automatically gain engineering controls.
Define:
role/permission model;

API authorization;

audit logging;

session behavior;

command confirmation requirements;

sensitive-data exclusions.

Never expose:
signing keys;

private keys;

wrapping keys;

raw secrets;

production credentials.

Propose the minimum additional schemas needed.
For each proposed schema include:
field

type

source

persistence requirement

retention requirement

whether required or optional

DiagnosticEventDeviceHealthSnapshotTransportObservationInstallationTestSessionInstallationTestStep

Avoid duplicating the product event database unnecessarily.
Propose APIs needed by the engineering UI.
Example categories:
GET devices/healthGET diagnostics/liveGET diagnostics/events/{id}GET diagnostics/devices/{id}POST diagnostics/devices/{id}/testPOST diagnostics/devices/{id}/identifyPOST diagnostics/devices/{id}/restartPOST diagnostics/devices/{id}/recommissionPOST installation-testsPOST installation-tests/{id}/steps
Do not treat these example names as mandatory.
First examine current API style and follow existing conventions.
For every endpoint define:
purpose

request

response

auth

error codes

data source

Analyze:
Hub RAM impact

Hub flash/NVS impact

C3 RAM/flash impact

radio overhead

backend storage

PWA memory

diagnostic event volume

Avoid continuously streaming unnecessary raw logs.
Recommend retention levels such as:
short live window;

bounded recent diagnostics;

longer-lived installation result;

aggregated health history.

Provide approximate sizing where the current system provides enough inputs.
Clearly mark assumptions.
Define diagnostic categories such as:
NODE_OFFLINEWEAK_RADIOASSOCIATION_FAILUREACK_TIMEOUTEXCESSIVE_RETRYDUPLICATE_EVENTHUB_STORAGE_FAILUREBACKEND_OFFLINEBACKEND_QUEUE_GROWINGCONFIG_MISMATCH
For each category provide:
evidence required;

likely subsystem;

severity;

operator message;

recommended next check.

Do not label something a root cause unless evidence proves it.
Design automated coverage for:
node online/offline

heartbeat expiry

RSSI update

product event trace

ACK/retry visibility

duplicate handling

backend offline

outbox backlog

reboot/rejoin

installation PASS

installation FAIL

wrong node triggered

timeout

technician authorization

caregiver authorization denial

simulator/real API contract consistency

event correlation

bounded diagnostic history

Identify:
unit tests

integration tests

simulator tests

Playwright tests

physical HIL tests

Do not modify the existing validation framework during this design task.
Propose implementation in small stages.
Example structure:
Stage 1Read-only telemetry + simulator
Stage 2Engineering overview + live events
Stage 3End-to-end event trace
Stage 4Guided installation test
Stage 5Controlled technician actions
Stage 6Physical HIL validation

For each stage state:
modules affected;

dependencies;

tests;

expected risk;

implement APIs;

implement UI;

change CMake;

# 2026-10-12 — USER-REQUESTED REACTIVATION / TONIGHT'S ENGINEERING DIAGNOSTICS DELIVERY PLAN

**Decision:** GS-120, GS-122, GS-124, GS-125 reactivated from OnHold to **To Do**, as sequenced linked workstream. This is **authorization to plan and begin design**, and user intent to implement/validate, NOT an approval of unreviewed production authorization/credential/retention/hardware operations. No code, tests, fixture operations, or Codex session was launched by Jira editing.

## Work ownership / stage gates

**GS-122 umbrella** — coordinate architecture, implementation, validation and end-to-end evidence; maintain actual delivery/approval status.
**GS-120 DESIGN FIRST** — perform source/requirements-based detailed UI, diagnostic model, event correlation, exact capability labels, minimal schema/API and role/permission assessment; produce architectural design, open decision register, threat/retention/budget, module/test map. This issue's DESIGN-ONLY prohibition remains valid within this issue; no source writes in GS-120 stage. The user may approve the resulting GS-120 design for GS-124; the existence of report or Jira To Do alone does not satisfy design approval.
**GS-124 IMPLEMENTATION SECOND** — start only after explicit GS-120 design acceptance (and only on approved subset). Prefer no-new-credential, read-only, bounded observational MVP: technician installation/overview, live events, event trace, device/comms health, correlated existing EventKey, guided installation test with exact-node PASS gating, reusable backend/PWA simulator contract. No new privileged Restart/Recommission/Test Control production endpoints without separate authorization and GS-109/GS-143 commercial auth policy. No second product event pipeline; no changing existing ACK, replay, registry, ownership or storage schema. Isolated branch/worktree and exclusive owned files; GS-148 remains active canonical writer.
**GS-125 VALIDATION THIRD, progressive during GS-124** — real production-code unit tests (positive/negative/boundaries), deterministic simulator, Node/Hub/API/PWA integration, browser/Playwright technician + caregiver denial, exact-event/full-product trace where components exist; dedicated HIL test mappings, permanent GS-116 suite registration/meta failure propagation, focused component/contract regression and source/evidence fingerprints. Whole release-gate-final/full validation-fast NOT_RUN until genuine RC or separate request. Existing legacy migration FAIL and GS-130 product PARTIAL must remain visible.
**GS-65** separate installer/engineering diagnostic contract; do not change its priority/status as a side effect.

## Hard prerequisites and stop conditions

(1) Read current AGENTS.md, canonical product/decision/release/validation contract, Jira GS-120/122/124/125/65/116/130/148/109/114, and source HEAD. GS-152 made `code/` ownership paths canonical. Detect GS-148 uncommitted modifications and do NOT copy/merge/overwrite them.  
(2) **Design approval gate:** before GS-124, present selected implementation contract and any approval-sensitive choices (telemetry provenance, technician roles, data retention/privacy, privileged commands, budget, backend auth). If unapproved, deliver GS-120 design and STOP that affected implementation or limit to independently safe approved component; never silently lock.  
(3) **Implementation isolation:** separate worktree/branch based on clean remote, with rebase-free/force-free push, no canonical merge while GS-148 writes. Preserve all untracked GS-114 evidence/managed_components/ and prior source/fixtures. No operations in protected physical C3/S3.  
(4) **Physical HIL gate:** GS-130 already provides `validation-board-hil` and `validation-motion-hil` opt-in runners and GS-116 physical release-evidence registry. They have NOT been current-head physically qualified. Existing S3 diagnostics/replay-fence failure and C3 USB_UART_CHIP_RESET have led to GS-114 physical NO-GO. Do NOT open/enumerate ports, flash, erase, reset, power-cycle, change pairing/eFuse/partitions/OTA or trigger physical stimuli without exact device/fixture and per-operation explicit user authorization plus safe no-reset/no-state-loss plan. If no approved independent disposable fixture/compatible running firmware, prepare HIL scripts/cases and report BLOCKED/NOT_RUN (never PASS). Synthetic INJECT_MOTION != optical PIR.  
(5) **Contract trust gate:** commercial technician roles/OIDC/Hub claim and related privileged control remain GS-109/GS-143 pending; GS-104 R01–R09 is unrelated and must not be enabled/implemented by the dashboard. Never trust QR/MAC/unverified self-declared telemetry as authorization. Backend/PWA development test identity is not commercial trust.  
(6) **GS-148 integration gate:** avoid new Hub persistent state schema, CloudSync receipt claims, live S3 outbox/journal modification or GC changes during GS-148 writer. When trace stage is unimplemented, present UNKNOWN/NOT_AVAILABLE, never fabricated PASS. Actual physical Node→backend→PWA qualification still owned by GS-117/121.  
(7) **Time/quota:** this is multi-stage work, likely beyond one model window/overnight. At each stage checkpoint commit only independently tested reviewed safe changes, source/hash/command/results, gaps. Don't mark GS-124/125/122 Done based on design, static tests, or runner registration.

## Implementation scope and concrete done criteria

Design covers: live technician overview, device detail, transport health/radio observations, Wi-Fi/backend/outbox state, timeline, event trace with sensor→C3→ESP-NOW→Hub authenticated validation→local durable state/ACK→backend durable COMMITTED→PWA observation; guided exact-device installation, timeout/wrong-node/duplicate and absence of overall PASS for untested mandatory nodes; evidence-grade UNKNOWN/STALE/NOT_APPLICABLE; explicit missing instrument/absence of person identity; dashboards never emit a medical claim or safety all-clear.  
QA covers: permission denial/cross-Home, no raw secrets, incomplete-stage unknown, Node offline/heartbeat with actual approved 300s/910s profile—not stale 190s; retries/lost ACK/deduplication; backend unavailable/recovery, storage blocked, timeline correct, pagination/backpressure/retention bounds, reset/session/ownership generation, real/sim API parity and caregiver unchanged. Use GS-116 feature/contract/release suite ownership and GS-130 149 features/200 modules + current 99-case physical catalogue; add stable new IDs only where genuinely missing, no duplicate framework.

**Stage outcomes expected separately:** GS120_DESIGN=PROPOSED/APPROVED, GS124_IMPLEMENTATION=PASS/PARTIAL/BLOCKED/NOT_STARTED, GS125_UNIT, SIM, INTEGRATION, PLAYWRIGHT, REGRESSION, GATE_REGISTRATION, BOARD_HIL, MOTION_HIL, REAL_PRODUCT_E2E each PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/NOT_RUN. Physical acceptance and full release distinct.

**Existing baseline:** GS-116 61-stage release registry, fast 50-stage union; GS-130 8 group/325 host board-stack PASS, P0 assertions 26/26+Chromium 1 PASS but product_status PARTIAL, 99 physical cases, 27 blocking: 3 PASS/3 PARTIAL/20 NOT_RUN/1 BLOCKED at recorded checkpoint. This plan does not overwrite those independent statuses.

**Next action:** user starts a dedicated Codex session using this staged plan. Jira alone does not schedule/run local Codex or HIL. No completion ETA/physical PASS is promised.

# CURRENT EXECUTION POLICY — 2026-10-11 (USER APPROVED; OVERRIDES OLDER BROAD-GATE INSTRUCTIONS)

**During implementation, bug fixing, simulation work, and ordinary feature/validation-framework tasks, DO NOT run** `make release-gate-final` or an unconditional full `make validation-fast`/full PWA-browser-backend campaign. Run **the new feature tests + ALL existing regressions of each affected component (C3 Node / S3 Hub / backend / PWA) + only affected cross-component/contract tests**, with relevant focused builds/sanitizers. Backend/PWA tests are required in the development loop only when their source, data model, or outward contract is affected. Preserve safety/security/durability regressions relevant to the changed board/component. Diagnose and report all selected-test failures; never suppress failing tests. Build/register relevant tests permanently into the complete release gate, and verify inclusion/failure propagation through lightweight registry/meta/dry-run checks, not expensive complete execution.

`release-gate-final` and the full product Node+Hub+integration+backend+PWA/browser suites must actually run at a genuine software/product release candidate, or upon separate explicit user request. A release/physical-qualification-specific ticket retains the exact dedicated acceptance tests it owns; this policy does not remove applicable physical/HIL, security/FOTA, or real backend/PWA contract acceptance. Mark unexecuted full gates **NOT_RUN / deferred to release candidate**, never PASS. The updated current user instruction controls if historical text below demands a full gate in each feature task. This is a validation-scope change, NOT a waiver of comprehensive regression coverage, a product-release approval, or permission to close a physically unverified ticket.

## 1. Component ownership and automatic impact classification

* **NODE SUITE** (C3): actual implemented features, including PIR sensing/first motion, activity burst/compaction, NodeHealth/JSON policy, PowerPolicy/light sleep/timer state machines, durable event admission/pending/retry/ACK retirement, security/rejoin, storage, FOTA and battery policy. A Node change MUST pass its new feature tests and ALL EXISTING relevant Node regressions, not only recently changed tests.
* **HUB SUITE** (S3): all Hub source/feature regressions: authenticated ESP-NOW reception, replay/dedupe, application Durable ACK, journal/reboot recovery, CloudSync/storage, liveness, FOTA/security, backend transport as implemented. Hub changes MUST pass new+existing Hub regressions.
* **NODE↔HUB CONTRACT SUITE**: run whenever one side changes on-wire or shared behavioral semantics (ACK/retry/rejoin, secure identity, NodeHealth offline contract, persistence/processing across the boundary); test both sides and compatibility, independent of a real board where deterministic host simulation can do so.
* **BACKEND/API/PWA SUITES**: run when directly modified OR when a changed Node/Hub contract affects UI/backend behaviors (coverage/offline, chronology, notification, settings, event identity). PWA is NOT an unconditional prerequisite for EVERY firmware-only developer change. Do not assume an unchanged PWA is unaffected by an altered contract.
* **FULL PRODUCT RELEASE SUITE**: on every release candidate, ALWAYS run all Node, Hub, cross-component integration, backend/API and PWA regression suites plus applicable security, durable recovery, FOTA, sanitizers, target builds and bounded stress. A component-only PASS is NEVER a full release PASS. Component-scoped developer gates should be efficient; complete release gate may be broader.

## 2. Executable test layers / ownership

1. **Change gate (fast, component-scoped):** feature-level deterministic unit/state-machine/negative/failure simulation; all previously implemented features in each affected component; cross-component tests when contract impacted. Must be reachable via named Node/Hub/integration targets (names selected after examining current Makefiles). No unrelated global PWA/browser run unless affected.
2. **validation-fast (project-wide):** mandatory cheap deterministic full component + interface suites with correct nonzero failure propagation and no silently missing new regressions. Implement as an aggregate of reusable component suites rather than hand-maintained duplicate lists; existing contractual fast coverage may include lightweight API/PWA and must not be weakened by this rule. Optimize unnecessary duplicate work.
3. **release-gate-final:** authoritative complete software/product candidate gate: Node+Hub+integration+backend/API+PWA + appropriate sanitizers, production builds, security/FOTA, bounded workload, configuration/traceability. MUST dominate validation-fast and fail for mandatory test failure, skipped mandatory stage, zero discovered tests, stale artifacts, missing build dependency or timeout. Do not confuse software-only PASS with physical product release approval.
4. **nightly/extended:** expensive simulations, stress, multi-node scale and long virtual soaks as needed; track mandatory prerelease cadence.
5. **physical/HIL:** REAL GPIO/PIR electrical wake, RF/ESP-NOW, sleep/current/power, real OTA boot/rollback, board/storage/powercut/endurance, and real C3→S3→backend→PWA when needed. Never infer physical PASS from host counters or compile success.

## 3. Permanent feature Definition of Done

For EACH story/code change, Codex and reviewer must determine: affected components/interfaces; existing relevant feature inventory and regression set; new positive/negative/error-recovery tests; fast/release/extended registration; physical/manual requirement; expected evidence owner/Jira.
**SOFTWARE_DELIVERED** only after: new feature tests PASS; full affected-component previous-feature suites PASS; relevant interface compatibility simulations PASS; eligible regressions permanently wired into validation-fast (or justified as release/extended); relevant build/sanitizer gates PASS; traceability and evidence documented; implementation committed/pushed and verified per project AGENTS. No feature should be called software-complete from an ad hoc focused test alone.
**FEATURE DONE / PHYSICALLY QUALIFIED** only if all required real-target/HIL/manual acceptance evidence is actually PASS on applicable final image/fixture, or an expressly approved and documented scope decision establishes physical testing is not required. Otherwise classify SOFTWARE_DELIVERED / PHYSICAL_NOT_RUN, BLOCKED, etc.; NEVER silently call it Done.
**RELEASE APPROVED** only after release-gate-final software PASS plus all applicable hardware/release gates and accepted outstanding-risk decisions. Zero/test skips, MANUAL_REQUIRED, old source HEAD, historical HIL, targeted test only, or unqualified board imagery are NOT release PASS.
**Regression rule:** Feature N implementation adds permanent tests for N and reruns **all prior relevant implemented features** in affected Node/Hub suites, plus interface tests where applicable. Fix discovered gaps instead of suppressing tests. Use deterministic virtual clock/fault injection for NodeHealth, light sleep, retries, ACK, power state, outages, FOTA and durability. Record honest environment/manual/physical limitations.
**Mandatory feature handoff:** component impact; affected interfaces; test ID→requirement→feature mapping; test commands and counts/exits; previous-feature regression results; effective firmware/config build profile; physical needed/PASS/NOT_RUN; precise software and release status; Jira owner; code/docs commit/push/remote HEAD; next prioritized Jira item.

summary: Implement trusted Add Device installer-to-Hub control path
description:
OBJECTIVE
Implement the trusted product control path that allows an authorizedinstaller/service/backend flow to instruct an installed Hub to add one exactphysical Node securely.
This is the missing product-side entry point into the already-implementedsecure commissioning machinery.
This is NOT a redesign of Node identity, commissioning cryptography, or runtimeHub-Node security.
============================================================BACKGROUND
Phase-2 already contains the secure commissioning foundation, including:
permanent Node identity

asymmetric Node identity/key material

exact expected Node identity

QR/public identity concept

authenticated commissioning

challenge/response identity proof

Hub/Home authorization foundation

ECDH

HKDF

persistent association

authenticated rejoin

Node registry

removal/revocation/replacement foundations

An internal exact-node commissioning API already exists on the Hub side.
The gap discovered during Phase-2 is that there is no real trusted productchannel from:
installer / service / backend        ->installed Hub        ->existing commissioning owner API
Therefore the product cannot yet expose a proper "Add Device" workflow withoutusing a test/HIL/internal caller.
We deliberately did NOT implement a hard-coded or insecure shortcut duringPhase-2.
============================================================PROBLEM TO SOLVE
Provide a real authenticated/authorized control path for a trusted actor torequest:
"Add this exact Node to this Home/Hub"
The request must carry enough identity context to pin the expected Node, forexample the QR/public identity already defined by the device identity model.
The Hub must then invoke the EXISTING secure commissioning path.
Do not duplicate commissioning cryptography in the product-control layer.
============================================================EXPECTED HIGH-LEVEL FLOW
Authorized installer/service/backend        |        vauthenticated control request        |        vHub validates authorization / Home ownership        |        vbounded commissioning window        |        vexact QR-pinned Node identity expected        |        vNode proves private identity        |        vHub/Home authentication        |        vECDH        |        vHKDF        |        vpersistent association        |        vlogical Node / room / function assignment        |        vplacement / communication verification        |        vREADY
============================================================SCOPE
Implement the product control-plane integration needed to invoke existingcommissioning safely.
Scope includes:
trusted Add Device request entry point

request authentication

authorization to manage the target Home/Hub

exact expected Node identity input

bounded commissioning request

result/status reporting

success/failure response

mapping to logical Node identity

room/function assignment if the current product workflow supports it

retry/timeout behavior

audit/event logging

safe cancellation

commissioning-in-progress state

protection against duplicate/concurrent Add Device requests

use of the existing Hub security/commissioning owner API

============================================================OUT OF SCOPE
Do NOT redesign:
Node asymmetric identity

ECDH

HKDF

runtime AEAD

replay protection

persistent association format

authenticated rejoin

FOTA

production manufacturing PKI

Secure Boot/eFuse

Do NOT create a second commissioning implementation.
============================================================SECURITY REQUIREMENTS
The Add Device request must fail closed.
Requirements:
only an authorized installer/service/user with manage permission may requestAdd Device

request must be bound to the intended Home/Hub

exact Node identity must be supplied/pinned

MAC address alone must NOT be treated as cryptographic identity

unknown/unexpected Nodes must be rejected

no universal production secret

no bypass of Node private-key proof

no exposure of runtime/session keys to installer/backend

bounded commissioning window

replay/duplicate request handling

cancellation/timeout must leave Hub in a safe state

commissioning failure must not silently admit a different Node

============================================================FAILURE CASES TO COVER
At minimum:
unauthorized requester

wrong Home

wrong Hub

wrong QR/public identity

unexpected Node appears

expected Node never appears

Node identity proof fails

commissioning timeout

duplicate Add Device request

concurrent Add Device request

Hub restart during commissioning

Node restart during commissioning

association persistence failure

registry full

already-enrolled Node

revoked Node

replacement-device flow if reused by Add/Replace

============================================================PRODUCT / UX RESULT
On success, product should be able to report something equivalent to:
Device addedNode identity verifiedAssociation storedRoom/function assignedDevice ready
On failure, return a specific reason rather than a generic pairing failure.
Do not claim successful installation until the persistent association and anyrequired readiness/placement check have completed.
============================================================IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE
Before coding:
Inspect the existing exact-node commissioning API.

Inspect current Hub security-owner ownership boundaries.

Inspect backend authorization / household manage permissions.

Inspect current installer/device-management UI/service paths.

Reuse existing APIs wherever possible.

Do not implement a new transport/protocol if an existing product/backendcontrol path can safely carry the request.
If the current backend/Hub control channel is development-only, define andimplement the smallest production-appropriate path.
============================================================ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
The feature is complete when an authorized product-side caller can:
identify the target Home/Hub

provide the exact expected Node public identity

request Add Device

cause the Hub to open a bounded commissioning operation

authenticate the expected Node

reject wrong/unknown Nodes

establish the existing secure association

persist the association

return success/failure state to the caller

leave the Node capable of normal authenticated rejoin afterward

Focused tests must cover:
success

unauthorized request

wrong identity

timeout

duplicate request

Hub restart/recovery

persistent association

normal post-commissioning authenticated communication

============================================================VALIDATION
Use:
host/unit tests first

target builds

focused physical commissioning only where real hardware behavior is required

Do NOT require broad HIL regression as part of this ticket.
Broad Phase-2 HIL requalification is tracked separately.
============================================================DOCUMENTATION
Update:
docs/features/DEVICE_IDENTITY_REGISTRATION_AND_LIFECYCLE.md
and any installer/service guide that becomes relevant.
Document:
product Add Device flow

authorization boundary

exact-node identity handling

failure semantics

source ownership

known limitations

============================================================DEFINITION OF DONE
DONE means:
real product-side Add Device entry point exists

authorization is enforced

exact Node identity is pinned

existing secure commissioning path is used

no security bypass is introduced

success/failure is reported to caller

persistent association is created

normal authenticated rejoin works afterward

focused tests pass

relevant documentation is updated

# CURRENT EXECUTABLE SCOPE — 2026-10-10 | GS-114 / GS-149 SPLIT (USER APPROVED)

**GS-114 is now the separate, closable BAT-C8 NON-POWER functional qualification owner (P1–P9 as applicable under the authoritative TEST_PLAN).** Existing BAT-C8 production software and host/target build are complete; this task does not reimplement them. **GS-149 exclusively owns BAT-C8 P10 quantitative power/energy acceptance** using results from existing GS-140/41/42/141/43/44/51 and GS-144. This split supersedes all earlier instructions in this issue implying GS-114 cannot close until P10/B0–B4/AFTER power measurements finish. GS-146 still owns final C1–C8 release gate.

**Acceptance for GS-114 alone:** using the canonical `docs/hw/evidence/BAT_C8_R1_QUALIFICATION/TEST_PLAN.md` and actual P1–P9 mapping, record source/image/hash/board/PIR GPIO4/power path and physical evidence for remaining non-power wake/runtime checks: real AM312 PIR activation, timer wake, multiple light-sleep transitions, session/ESP-NOW restore, authenticated Hub durable ACK, retry/lost-ACK/EventKey safety, Hub absence/return/rejoin, required FOTA/control/persistence sleep inhibitors and no unexplained reset/stall. Reuse valid dated evidence only if image/fixture provenance matches. Disposition all assigned cases as PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/NOT_RUN with traceable logs; do not claim energy/lifetime savings. **GS-46** owns dedicated first-event latency gate, **GS-69** owns 12-hour soak and end PIR->ACK, **GS-119** owns residual C1–C4; cite their accepted evidence, do not duplicate tests. If canonical TEST_PLAN contains a measurement subcase under P1–P9, move its quantified acceptance to GS-149 without silently dropping it.

**Independent closure:** GS-114 can be closed once its NON-POWER assigned evidence is accepted, even while GS-149, GS-51, GS-46, GS-69 or GS-146 remain open. GS-149 separately blocks GS-146. Maintain approved hardware safety: no protected S3/original paired C3 flash, reset, erase, repartition or re-enrollment without explicit approval. Only use `~/projects/Ghar_sajag_r1` branch `feature/r1-commercial-baseline`.

## Historical GS-114 description below (implementation and planning provenance; conflicts with above split are superseded)

---

## CURRENT BATTERY PRIORITY — 10 OCT 2026 | RESUME R1 C8 PHYSICAL QUALIFICATION

**Status:** BAT-C8 software, focused host validation and qualification image build are ALREADY COMPLETE per Jira; next focus is **remaining physical P1–P10 and B0–B4/AFTER power measurements**, not reimplementation. S3 GS-148/GS-131 moved to OnHold after P2-D partial pushed checkpoint due to unresolved production security/workload contracts. Jira progress/handoff: GS-114 comment 10310; GS-148 comment 10308. No hardware testing has been newly executed by this ticket update.

**Immediate BAT-C8 steps:** Verify correct battery R1 worktree branch/HEAD and canonical AGENTS.md/qualification plan; reuse valid AM312 GPIO4 PIR->Node->authenticated Hub->ACK and past outage evidence. Close only outstanding physical GPIO4/timer wake, first-event latency, sleep inhibitors during ACK/rejoin/OTA, Hub outage/recovery, GS-69 12h soak with END real PIR, GS-119 remaining C1–C4, GS-140 repeatable current setup/B1–B4 BEFORE and GS-51 AFTER/P10 matched power, GS-144 numeric battery-life target and reproducible workload, GS-146 C1–C8 physical release gate. Record actual measured evidence/limitations; do not claim battery savings from counters. Any protected S3/paired C3 flash/reset/re-enrollment is forbidden without user approval.

**FOLLOWING BAT-C8:** GS-115 C9 conditional low-battery warning/QoS with real measurement hardware, C10 flash-write measurement before change, C11 default post-R1 fixed TX unless RF/power data justify adaptive change, C12 deep sleep only after measured target gap. GS-115 stays To Do; no automatic C9–C11 code changes.

---

This is probably the **largest actual battery-life improvement**, but deliberately comes after the policies and counters.

The current target has no sleep/wake-source integration yet.

**Design**

```
PIR continuously powered

quiet + safe-to-sleep
        ↓
PowerPolicy approves sleep
        ↓
C3 LIGHT SLEEP
        ↓
GPIO4 PIR / required timer wake
        ↓
resume runtime
        ↓
first motion immediately processed
        ↓
radio/event work
        ↓
ACK/recovery complete
        ↓
return to light sleep
```

Deep sleep is explicitly **not** part of this Story.

‌

Codex:      
BAT-C8 — AUTOMATIC LIGHT SLEEP + GPIO4 PIR WAKE

Prerequisites:

BAT-C1/C2 measurement/policy foundation      
BAT-C3/C4/C5 traffic/retry/health policies      
BAT-C6 burst behavior stable enough not to conflict with sleep

Do NOT implement deep sleep.

# ============================================================

TARGET

Integrate ESP32-C3 light sleep under PowerPolicy ownership.

PIR remains continuously powered.

Use GPIO4 as wake source only after confirming target/ESP-IDF support and      
electrical behavior.

Also support required timer/control/retry deadlines safely.

# ============================================================

SLEEP ELIGIBILITY

Never sleep while:

* commissioning/rejoin active
* FOTA/control active
* immediate critical event pending
* TX/ACK transaction requiring progress
* durable persistence incomplete
* required retry deadline would be missed
* runtime state cannot safely resume

# ============================================================

WAKE

On PIR wake:

* capture wake reason
* process first qualified motion promptly
* do not lose PIR state during transition
* preserve authentication/session semantics
* resume radio safely

# ============================================================

HISTORICAL REGRESSION

Explicitly test the historical condition where motion detection previously      
stopped until re-plug.

Long idle      
→ sleep/wake cycles      
→ repeated PIR events      
→ continued sensing

must remain reliable without physical re-plug.

# ============================================================

INSTRUMENTATION

Populate BAT-C1 counters:

* awake time
* light-sleep time
* wake count
* wake reason
* sleep-prevention reason

# ============================================================

VALIDATION

Host/state-machine tests first.

C3 target build.

Then minimum focused real-hardware validation:

* real PIR wake
* long idle
* repeated sleep/wake
* first-motion latency
* authenticated event ACK after wake
* Hub outage/recovery
* FOTA/maintenance sleep inhibition
* no unexpected reset
* no motion-stall regression

Measure current/battery behavior against the current-HEAD baseline.

No broad HIL.

Return:

SLEEP_DESIGN      
GPIO4_WAKE      
SLEEP_INHIBITORS      
WAKE_LATENCY      
MOTION_RELIABILITY      
SESSION_BEHAVIOR      
POWER_MEASUREMENT      
TESTS      
PHYSICAL_EVIDENCE      
COMMIT
